title: Flyway or Liquibase for database migration

videos.script: Since lesson 9 your tables have come from one file, schema.sql. It runs on every start, and it says: create the table if it does not exist. {{schema}} That works until the table exists and has to change. Then the file says one thing, the database says another, and nothing tells you. {{drift}} A migration tool replaces the file with a list of changes. Each change is a numbered file. Each runs once, in order, and the database records that it ran. {{versions}} In this lesson the bookshop moves to Flyway. You read the history table it keeps, and you watch it refuse to start when somebody edits a file that already ran. {{history}} Hibernate stops guessing the schema and starts checking it, and the first check finds a real mismatch. {{validate}} Then you write a migration that fails halfway, and watch PostgreSQL take all of it back. {{rollback}} And you run the same tables through Liquibase, the other tool Spring Boot supports, to see what it does differently. {{liquibase}}
